To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) wearing a surgical mask affects the acoustical characteristics of the speech signal, (b) the phonetic context is important for the detection of masked speech and (c) the intelligibility of the speech signal is affected by the wearing of the mask

(a) phonemes are affected by the mask wearing in different ways depending on their place of articulation, (b) phonetic context and phoneme intelligibility are important factors for the mask detector, and (c) the mask detector performance can be improved by combining phonetic context and bottom up approaches.

(1) the most affected phonemes when wearing masks are /p, t, k, m, f, v/; (2) the most affected segments are those containing the phonemes /p, t/; (3) the most affected vowels are /i, u, o/; (4) the intelligibility of masked speech is significantly lower (about 10% on average); (5) the phonetic mask detector is more efficient than the frame clustering method
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and detection of speech changes due to wearing a mask.
the detection of masked speech in a binary classification problem and the analysis of the effects of mask-wearing on the speech production system.
a better understanding of the speech changes caused by the mask wearing, and how these changes can be detected.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a mask affects the intelligibility of the speech signal and that the most affected segments are those containing fricatives.
the phonetic context and the intelligibility are important features for the mask detection task, and that the phonetic analysis is a promising approach to improve the mask detection performance.
mask wearing affects the intelligibility of speech in German language, and the phonetic context of the spoken sentence has an impact on the detection performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mask wearing has a significant impact on the phonetic and perceptual properties of the speech signal.
phonetic context and frame clustering are the most relevant factors for a good mask detector performance.
mask wearing has a negative impact on intelligibility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phoneme-based mask detector is the most efficient mask detector on the MSCC and MASC, and that the frame clustering mask detector is the second most efficient on the MSCC.
the phonetic context and the phonetic analysis of the signal can be useful for the development of a mask detector.
a bottom up approach is more efficient than a large composite feature approach for this type of task.
